title: Service credit, degradation tiers, and escalation contract for private deployments
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary

Purpose: This document defines a standardized contract used by Redwood and customers operating Private (VPC or on‑prem) deployments to apply service credits when platform behavior falls below defined SLOs. It covers degradation tier definitions, measurement windows, credit-calculation rules, operator actions required to validate incidents, and the escalation and dispute-handling process.

Scope
- Applies to customer Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem) where Redwood provides control plane services, runtime updates, or remote operator support per the signed customer contract.
- Not intended for customer-managed operational errors (see Exclusions).

Definitions
- Availability SLO: Percent of successful request completions measured at the request router (ingress).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end response time for generation requests measured at the ingress proxy.
- Degradation Window: Continuous 60-minute internal window used for short-window credit triggers; longer windows are noted below.
- Major Degraded State: Service state where availability < 95% or latency p95 > configured threshold for >= 4 hours.
- Critical Outage: Total control plane unreachability or tenant request loss >= 99% for a contiguous 30-minute window.

SLOs and Degradation Tiers
| Tier | Trigger (measurement source) | Time window | SLO breach condition | Service credit |
|-----|-----------------------------|-------------:|----------------------|---------------:|
| Minor | Ingress SLIs (edge proxy) | 1 hour | Availability < 99.5% | 2% monthly invoice cap |
| Moderate | Ingress + Runtime telemetry | 4 hours | Availability < 98% OR p95 latency > target by >= 50% | 5% monthly invoice cap |
| Major | Aggregated platform SLIs (control plane + data plane) | 24 hours | Availability < 95% OR sustained error spike > 10% | 15% monthly invoice cap |
| Critical | Business-impacting outage detected by oncall or customer signal | 30 minutes contiguous | Control plane unreachable OR persistent tenant request loss >=99% | 30% monthly invoice cap |

Measurement and Sources
- Primary source: Redwood telemetry ingestion from customer-deployed telemetry agents and the Redwood control plane. For air-gapped installs the operator-provided telemetry bundle (see Evidence bundle) is used.
- SLIs are computed by the measurement job defined in /ops/slo-rules.yml (example below). Measurements that rely exclusively on customer-side telemetry require the customer telemetry attestation in the Evidence bundle.

Example SLI rule (YAML snippet)
---
- name: private_ingress_availability
  source: edge-proxy
  metric: successful_requests / total_requests
  window: 60m
  aggregation: sliding_window
  threshold: 0.995
---

Credit Calculation Rules
1. Credits are applied against the affected month’s invoice and cannot exceed the monthly cap shown in the table above.
2. If multiple tiers are triggered in the same billing month, credits stack up to a maximum of 50% of the monthly invoice unless otherwise limited by contractual terms.
3. Credits are calculated pro rata when an affected tenant is a subset of the customer deployment. Example calculation: credit = monthly_charge_for_affected_tenant * applicable_credit_percentage * (affected_minutes / total_minutes_in_month).
4. Credits are issued only after validation and evidence receipt as described in the Evidence bundle section.

Evidence bundle (required for any credit claim)
- Incident timeline with UTC timestamps and owner notes.
- Aggregated SLI time series (CSV or Prometheus exposition format).
- Control plane logs covering the incident window (redacted for customer-sensitive fields).
- Configuration snapshot (runtime config, routing tables, model pinning) at start and end of incident window.
- For on‑prem/airgapped installs: signed telemetry attest document from customer operator (PGP-signed).

Operator validation checklist (run by Redwood incidents team within 48 hours)
1. Confirm timestamps and verify ingestion integrity (no duplicates or missing windows).
2. Cross-validate customer- and platform-reported SLIs. If discrepancy > 3% absolute, trigger forensic data capture.
3. Identify root cause class: platform, operator change, customer config, third‑party network.
4. If root cause is platform/operator, mark eligible and calculate credit using pro rata rules.

Exclusions (non-eligible credit triggers)
- Customer misconfiguration affecting routing, auth, or model artifacts where operator did not make changes within the incident window.
- Scheduled maintenance with 72h prior notification per contract.
- Third-party provider failure outside Redwood-owned control plane where customer has signed separate connectivity SLAs.

Escalation and Communication Protocols
- Initial acknowledgement: Redwood support owner will acknowledge customer-submitted credit request within 24 hours and provide a ticket number and primary contact.
- Investigation timeline: Standard investigation completes within 5 business days. Complex forensic investigations may extend to 30 days; customers will be notified of expected timelines.
- Weekly status updates for investigations longer than 5 business days.
- Decision and credit issuance: Once validation completes, Redwood issues a credit note applied to next invoice cycle and shares the Evidence bundle summary.

Escalation matrix (roles & SLAs)
- Support Engineer (Triage) — ack within 24h, initial findings within 48h.
- Incident Lead (Platform) — appointed within 48h for Moderate or above.
- Head of SRE/Platform Operations — engaged within 72h for Major/Critical incidents.
- VP Customer Success — engaged within 5 business days for disputes or >10% invoice credits.

Dispute resolution
1. Customer submits dispute with Evidence bundle within 30 days of credit decision.
2. Redwood and customer jointly appoint up to two technical reviewers each to re-evaluate the evidence. Review window: 15 business days.
3. If reviewers disagree, an independent third-party auditor (pre-approved in contract) will adjudicate. Auditor findings are binding for credit calculation only.

Operator runbook excerpts (quick steps for oncall)
1. Collect SLI series from metrics-backend: curl -sS "https://metrics.internal/api/series?from=START&to=END&name=private_ingress_availability" > incident-series.json
2. Export router traces: rtr-export --start TIME --end TIME --service tenant-123 > router-traces.ndjson
3. Capture runtime config: rdctl snapshot-config --tenant tenant-123 --out config-YYYYMMDD.json
4. Bundle evidence: tar czf evidence-INCIDENTID.tgz router-traces.ndjson incident-series.json config-YYYYMMDD.json controlplane-logs.tgz

Billing and Credit Issuance
- Credits are reflected as invoice line items titled "Service Credit — Private Deployment SLA" and reduce the next invoice amount by the calculated credit.
- Credits are not redeemable for cash unless explicitly stated in the customer contract.

Change control and review cadence
- This contract and thresholds are reviewed quarterly by Finance-Legal, Platform SRE, and Customer Success.
- Any change to SLO thresholds or credit caps requires a 30-day notice to customers and an update to the customer contract addendum.

Appendix A — Sample SLA clause (for contracts)
"Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Services available in accordance with the Availability SLOs defined in the Service Credit Schedule. If Redwood fails to meet the SLOs and Customer submits a validated credit claim per the Evidence bundle requirements, Redwood will issue Service Credits as specified in the Service Credit Schedule, subject to the exclusions and caps set forth in this Agreement."

Appendix B — Contact templates
- Initial acknowledgement email (template):
Subject: [INCIDENT #{INCIDENT_ID}] Acknowledgement — Private Deployment SLA Claim
Body: We have received your SLA credit request and opened ticket #{INCIDENT_ID}. Primary owner: {NAME}. Expected initial findings: within 48 hours.

- Closure email (template):
Subject: [INCIDENT #{INCIDENT_ID}] SLA Claim Decision and Credit Issuance
Body: Investigation complete. Root cause: {ROOT_CAUSE_CLASS}. Credit applied: {PERCENTAGE} resulting in credit amount {AMOUNT}. Evidence bundle summary attached.

Owners and review history
- Primary owners: Finance-Legal (contract), Platform SRE (measurement and validation), Customer Success (customer communications).
- Document owners: Maya Patel (Finance-Legal) — maintainer.
- Revision log: 2026-02-15 created by Maya Patel; 2026-06-01 updated credit stacking rules and evidence requirements (reviewers: Omar Ruiz, Priya Nair).

Related implementation artifacts
- ops/slo-rules.yml (measurement job definitions)
- ops/evidence-schema.md (evidence bundle format)
- infra/telemetry-agent/attestation-protocol.md (onprem attestation steps)

Notes and operational considerations
- For private deployments that mirror hosted telemetry, measurement should prefer platform-ingested SLIs to avoid inconsistent client-side sampling.
- In air-gapped installs Redwood recommends a weekly automated evidence snapshot to simplify forensic validation.
- When designing customer onboarding runbooks, include a short session explaining what qualifies as customer-managed vs Redwood-managed causes to minimize disputes.

If you have questions about how this contract maps to a specific customer agreement, contact the document owner or the Platform SRE lead for a technical review.
